focus: Spec Kit Memory MCP path resolution
noveltyJustification: The Memory MCP audit exposed canonical-first document discovery and an inconsistent recovery/repair boundary, distinct from the earlier tooling, Git, and mirror findings.
keyQuestions: How does Spec Kit Memory resolve spec paths, and what boundary changes would it require?
answeredQuestions: How does Spec Kit Memory resolve spec paths, and what boundary changes would it require?
ruledOutDirections: Treating Memory MCP as uniformly dual-root-aware across discovery, recovery, and repair.

finding: Spec identity and broad path classification accept both .opencode/specs and specs roots, with canonical-pair preference when both appear.

Memory document and graph-metadata discovery scans .opencode/specs when it exists and falls back to specs only when the canonical root is absent; realpath deduplication collapses a compatibility symlink.
Explicit indexing, generic base discovery, resume, and the maintained resolver inventory support both roots or direct paths, but precedence varies across the resolver call sites.
Pending recovery scans both roots while startup drift-marker and moved-folder recovery accept only .opencode/specs, creating a canonical-only blind spot after relocation.
Alias conflict analysis and canonical-path realpath handling support a transition bridge but do not make two independent roots discoverable simultaneously.
Graph repair defaults to .opencode/specs, and the context-server description refresh supplies that same old root as the generator base; both require a migration decision when the bridge is removed.
